prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1286; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports vehicles made contact at low speed in the travel lane. Police report not filed; both drivers exchanged information at scene. Claimant reports back strain and has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through attorney of record.

Entry 2: Received notice of representation from claimant's attorney. Letter of protection requested for medical treatment. Liability appears probable based on insured's statement and damage pattern. Requested itemized medical records and prior treatment history for lumbar region through counsel.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage inspected. Front bumper and grille damage on insured vehicle, rear bumper deformation on claimant vehicle. Damage consistent with reported low-speed impact. Photos uploaded to file. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop.

Entry 4: Attorney's office provided initial treatment summary. Claimant diagnosed with lumbar strain, prescribed physical therapy and muscle relaxants. Reviewed record for pre-existing back complaints; none found in the last several years. Medical bill review referred to nurse reviewer.

Entry 5: Discussed settlement posture with supervisor. Pending completion of treatment and receipt of final bills, file to remain open. Diary set for follow-up with claimant's counsel. Reserve adjusted to reflect probable liability and anticipated medical specials.
